gaps.gap: COMPOSITION. Each lane checks one claim against one body. No lane covers a false claim built from several docstrings, each true of its own body, whose combined behaviour breaks what a docstring or page promises. The lens set assumes a claim's truth can be settled locally. Exclusivity and consequence claims ('only because', 'cannot', 'so that') are settled only across the call graph.
gaps.evading_example: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:25 (gate_or_skip docstring): the build is skipped 'only because a round of a docs instrument is open'. Its body skips whenever docs_build_skipped is non-empty. src/DocLints.jl:45 returns frozen_rounds(...) whenever `code == 1` and GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP is unset, which is exactly what its own docstring says. src/CLI/Gate.jl returns the same exit 1 for two other problems: 'the fixes were committed without the round' (Gate.jl:21-22, 55-58) and 'an open round of the DISABLED instrument (CFG.VALID)' (Gate.jl:48-50). frozen_rounds (Gate.jl:84-85) has no enabled check and no dirty-tree check. In both cases the docs build prints 'makedocs: SKIPPED' and exits 0. TestHarness.gate() (src/TestHarness.jl:606) gates only 'bug-hunt' and 'audit-changes'. So a /check-docs round whose fixes were committed without the round passes both commit gates the package has, the docs build and Pkg.test(). Only a bare `gbg gate` would fire. docs/src/guide/rounds.md ends 'so a fix pass cannot be committed around an open round'. The index.md paragraph on the frozen build and the gate docstring's 'exit 1: the fixes were committed without the round' promise the same protection, and it does not hold for the doc instruments.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: rationale: reads ARCHITECTURE only; nothing here is a formula or a count. pages: rounds.md's 'cannot be committed around' is a consequence claim. Discharging it needs a trace across Gate.jl, DocLints.jl, the ext and TestHarness.jl, and the lane's CORRECT list (formula, constant, relation, complexity, quantifier) does not ask for a trace. src: gate's, frozen_rounds' and docs_build_skipped's docstrings are each accurate. ext: gate_or_skip's body is literally 'skip if docs_build_skipped non-empty', which matches its docstring unless the reader opens two src files and reasons about gate's full problem set. built-html: every blurb matches its @docs block. workflow-scripts, catalogues, rulebook, templates, schemas: off-object. family: no f/f! pair is involved. cold-reader: every term is defined. operational-claims: its unit is 'a docstring and ITS body'. All three docstring/body pairs agree; the falsity exists only in their conjunction.
gaps.proposed_lens: A claim-trace lane: enumerate every docstring or page sentence carrying an exclusivity or consequence operator ('only', 'never', 'cannot', 'so that', 'except'). For each, follow the calls it depends on to their leaves across files, and state the full set of inputs that reach the claimed outcome.

gaps.gap: NEGATIVE SPACE OF THE UNIVERSE. The lanes' `reads` lists are the lens set's whole domain, and no lens checks that they cover the documentation that exists. Tracked prose outside every list is never read: CLAUDE.md (loaded into every session; the project CLAUDE.md says AI is this package's main reader), README.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, CHANGELOG.md, the prose docs/make.jl prints into three generated pages, .github/workflows comments, and the source of instruments/*/PROTOCOL.md (reachable only as rendered HTML, under a built-html directive aimed at API blocks). It also breaks ARCHITECTURE D12's rule that finished work is not kept in CLAUDE.md. gaps.proposed_lens: A universe check in preflight: take the tracked text files, subtract the union of every lane's `reads`, print the rest, and have bank refuse unless each leftover file is in a declared exclusion list with a reason. Add a 'session-context' lane over CLAUDE.md, README.md and the generating prose in docs/make.jl, with git tags, bin/ and IMPLEMENTATION.md as ground truth.

gaps.gap: OVERLAP vs GAP on closed vocabularies. A contract stated on one surface (the exit codes, called 'the contract' in CLAUDE.md) and the one code site that breaks it sit on different surfaces, so they fall between the per-surface lanes. The family lane is the only relational lens, and its relation (f/f!, getter/set_!, physical/spectral) is empty in this package, whose `!` functions have no non-! twins. The relations that do exist here are left unowned: a vocabulary stated on several surfaces, and a verb's docstring against its page and its protocol.

Checking a category label means enumerating every 'refused' site across 26 CLI files, and the first four it samples confirm the claim; the single counterexample is on the src surface. src: gate's docstring and body agree on exit 1. ext: not involved. rationale: not the stating surface. operational-claims: gate's docstring matches gate's body; verbs.md is not a docstring. cold-reader: 'refused' is ordinary English carrying a package meaning, its specialty, but its substrate is exported docstrings and neither gate nor verbs.md is one. family: no pair. built-html, workflow-scripts, catalogues, rulebook, templates, schemas: none holds verbs.md and Gate.jl together.
gaps.proposed_lens: Replace the family lane's empty relation for this package with a vocabulary-contract lane: for each closed vocabulary (exit codes, closure channels, verdicts, doctor ids), collect every surface's statement of it and every code site that emits a member, and check them as one set. gaps.gap: The instrument fixes the truth referent at src/ and asks each lane for a quoted 'decisive line'. That leaves a whole class unjudged: claims whose truth is settled somewhere other than src/. That includes ext/, bin/gbg, docs/make.jl, and the git/CI workflow, which no file represents. It also leaves consequence claims unjudged ('X, so Y cannot happen'). For those, the lane finds a src line that confirms the premise X and never tests the consequence Y. A line that DETECTS a condition is also easily quoted as proof that the condition is PREVENTED. That is an object-versus-representation error, which check 1 names only for physics objects.

gaps.proposed_lens: A truthmaker lens over the pages surface. For each claim about behaviour, name WHERE its truth is decided (src/, ext/, bin/, docs/make.jl, templates/, CI/git/Pkg behaviour) and discharge it there. For every 'so / therefore / cannot / always' consequence, discharge the consequence itself, not its premise. A quoted line must PREVENT the thing asserted as impossible, not merely DETECT it. In practice: extend operational-claims from docstrings to guide pages, and make the lane's ground truth the whole repository plus the named external systems.

gaps.gap: Nothing in the default configuration can show that /check-docs missed something. Seeding is off for check-docs by default. A lane's coverage is attested only by its own checked[] list, and the brief tells lanes that an empty findings list with a non-empty checked[] is 'a real and useful result'. So a miss looks exactly like a clean surface. Where seeding exists (check-consistency, §6.4), seeds come from a catalogue the same author writes. Seeded recall therefore measures recall over the author's hypothesised classes, the very classes the lanes were written for. And the owner, per CLAUDE.md, does not review this package's pages, so the human channel is absent too.
gaps.evading_example: src/CLI/Preflight.jl:687-688 turns check-docs seeding on only if `get(dcfg, "seed_rounds", false)`, and src/CLI/Init.jl:160 writes `"seed_rounds" => false`. With the stale rounds.md:55 present through three check-docs-03 fix passes and the rc.6 commit, every lane that held rounds.md could return checked=["rounds.md"], findings=[]. Bank would classify it as a live lane, and grade would close the round. No artefact of the instrument records that the page still states a guarantee the code withdrew one day after writing it. I cannot see the round records under .gbg/rounds/, so I cannot say whether some lane raised it and it was carried or deferred. The instrument's own outputs give no way to tell, and that is the point.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: This is not a per-lane miss but a property of the verdict each lane emits. rationale, pages, src, ext, built-html, workflow-scripts, catalogues, rulebook, templates, schemas: each reports findings[] plus a self-declared checked[], with no planted item whose absence from findings[] would count against it. family, cold-reader, operational-claims: same output contract, and no seed targets their classes. The act verifier and state verifier grade only ids that exist. A defect that was never raised has no id, so neither verifier can grade it.
gaps.proposed_lens: No lens — needs a different mechanism: an out-of-hypothesis falsifier. One option is mutation replay of real history: for each mechanism-changing commit since the last round (e.g. ad7f832), re-apply the code change while reverting its doc edits, then score whether the lanes find every stale restatement. Another is a held-out, human-recorded findings set for check-docs, as `gbg calibrate` provides for check-consistency. Either way, recall must be measured on classes the lane author did not write.

gaps.gap: The instrument measures something other than what this package's trusting reader needs. That reader, by the package's own CLAUDE.md (RULE.DOC.AI_BANNER note: 'AI is this package's main reader'), is an AI session in a consumer. It reads guide pages, the rendered policy and the home page, and ACTS on them: whether it may push during a round, which version `gbg` is running, what exit 0 means. Its predicate is 'if I act on this sentence, the system behaves as stated, and the pages do not tell me two incompatible things'. The lenses measure per-file correspondence to src plus rubric form. The cold-reader stands in for the audience, but it is a human REPL user reading exported docstrings with the design docs withheld, not the actual reader or substrate.
gaps.evading_example: A consumer session reads docs/src/index.md:26-29 (an open docs round 'freezes the package's docs build … exit 0') and docs/src/guide/rounds.md:52-55 ('so a fix pass cannot be committed around an open round'). Each sentence can be matched to some code line: the first to DocLints.jl:45, the second's premise to Gate.jl's `return 1`. They are incompatible as action guides. A session that trusts rounds.md believes the docs build is a commit barrier during /check-docs. It then pushes fixes outside the round's pass/grade cycle, the CI docs job prints SKIPPED and exits green, and docs/make.jl:81 silently skips deploydocs. Similarly, install.md's 'always runs that consumer's pinned version' tells the session it need not check which copy ran after a bump.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: cold-reader: its substrate is exported docstrings via `?name` with design docs withheld, so guide pages and the home page are not in it. Its test is 'term used before defined', not 'instruction that misleads if obeyed'. operational-claims: docstrings only. pages: checks each file against src/ and against the formatting and citation rubric, with no cross-page consistency check and no 'what would a reader do with this' check. rationale, src, ext, built-html, workflow-scripts, catalogues, rulebook, templates, schemas: none reads both index.md and rounds.md, and none is asked about reader action. family: pairs of functions, not pairs of pages.
gaps.proposed_lens: A consumer-agent reader lane. Its persona is the actual reader: an AI session in a consumer holding only the rendered site and .gbg/policy. It reads the guide in nav order, lists every action-guiding sentence (may / cannot / always / exit N means …), checks each against the repository and the other pages, and reports contradictions between pages and instructions that fail when obeyed.

gaps.gap: The lens vocabulary was carried over from the physics consumers, so several positive procedures pass vacuously here. Checks 1, 3, 4 and 6 enumerate formulas, normalization constants, adjoint relations and house glyphs. The family lane enumerates f/f! and getter/set_! pairs and 'physical/spectral variant pairs'. In this package those sets are empty or nearly so. A procedure over an empty enumeration is satisfied trivially and still returns a non-empty checked[]. Meanwhile the package's real relational families go unenumerated: one mechanism restated in several homes, and the CLI-face/function pairs.

The family lane's enumeration is therefore empty by construction every round. The package's real family, the frozen-build skip rule, has six correct homes: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:22-29 (gate_or_skip), src/DocLints.jl:20-32 (makedocs), src/DocLints.jl:37-42 (docs_build_skipped), src/CLI/Gate.jl:71-78 (frozen_rounds), docs/src/index.md:26-29 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:491-494. It also has a seventh home that drifted, rounds.md:55. This is exactly the 'formula duplicated, one copy drifted' defect the family lane exists for, but the family lane has no way to enumerate it.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: family: enumerates f/f! and getter/setter pairs, finds none, reports clean. The relation 'same concept, N homes' is not in its enumeration. rationale, pages, src, ext: each sees only its own homes, and each copy it sees is individually true or unchecked, as shown in gap 1. cold-reader, operational-claims: docstrings, and each docstring copy is correct. built-html, workflow-scripts, catalogues, rulebook, templates, schemas: none of them hold a copy.
gaps.proposed_lens: Re-parameterise the family lane per package. Here its object should be 'one mechanism, all restatements': for each mechanism changed in the diff since the last round, grep the whole repository, excluding .gbg, for its terms, list every restatement, and verify each against the one home. Also treat cmd_<verb>/<verb> pairs as a family.

gaps.gap: The instrument treats the status quo as normative: 'GROUND TRUTH is src/'. It therefore has no verdict 'the page is right and the code regressed'. When the design, the rule and the code disagree, a finding is resolved by rewriting prose to match the code, and the act/state verifiers mark it HONORED. The last textual trace of an intended guarantee can be erased that way. The verifiers are the same kind of agent under the same framing, so that shared premise is invisible to all of them.
gaps.evading_example: I could not find a real instance in this tree where the code is wrong and the prose is right. In the case I examined (rounds.md:55 against the skip), the code, ARCHITECTURE.md:491 and the ext comment agree: the skip was a deliberate decision, recorded with its evidence ('25 in a row' red runs). Only the page is stale. I am reporting the conceptual gap without a demonstrated harmful instance, as the task permits.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: Every surface lane is told to verify prose against src/, so a code regression reads as a prose defect. family and cold-reader have no normative referent at all. operational-claims holds the docstring and the body together but is told to discharge the docstring against the body, never the reverse. Only the rulebook lane compares against policy, and it is aimed at rules, not at code.
gaps.proposed_lens: No lens — needs a different mechanism. When a claim disagrees with the code, a finding should record which referent it contradicts (code, ARCHITECTURE decision, or RULE id), and the fix pass should be barred from resolving a design- or rule-backed claim by editing the prose alone.

gaps.gap: A claim that is true for one member of a collective referent and false for another. "The deep doctor" means six checks. The brief's procedure (verify against src/ and quote the decisive line) is satisfied by the first line that confirms the claim. No lane is told to enumerate the members of the collective and check each one. The claim also sits in docstrings whose own bodies never touch the behaviour they describe.
gaps.evading_example: LIVE, in six homes: docs/src/index.md:29, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:494, src/DocLints.jl (makedocs docstring: "which is how `gbg release` and the deep doctor run it"), src/CLI/Gate.jl:77 (frozen_rounds docstring), and the comment in ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl. Each says the deep doctor sets `GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP`, turning the frozen-build skip back into a refusal. Only SELF.DOCS does it (src/CLI/Doctor.jl:643, `addenv(..., "GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP" => "1")`), and SELF.DOCS returns NA outside the tool root. BUILD.DOCS, the deep check every consumer runs (Doctor.jl:634-638), calls `shell(ctx.cfg["package"]["docs_build"])` with no such variable. It PASSes on exit 0 plus the banner `GBGCodingTools v… makedocs`. The ext prints that banner on its first line, before `gate_or_skip`, and a skipped build then returns nothing, exit 0. Consequence: in a consumer with an open /check-docs round, `gbg doctor --deep` reports `PASS BUILD.DOCS docs build exit 0 with the makedocs banner` although nothing was built. The docs tell the reader this cannot happen. CHANGELOG.md:452 alone has it right ("the deep doctor's `SELF.DOCS`"), and no lane reads CHANGELOG.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: rationale: reads ARCHITECTURE.md:494. It verifies against src/, and `rg GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP src/CLI/Doctor.jl` returns the SELF.DOCS addenv line, a deep check that sets it. That decisive quote confirms the claim, so the check is discharged. pages: same grep for index.md:29, same confirming line. The CORRECT check's quantifier list (exact/all/never/bit-for-bit) has no entry for an unquantified collective like "the deep doctor". src: it reads Gate.jl and DocLints.jl, runs the same grep and gets the same confirmation. Refuting it takes three facts from three places: the banner's position in the ext, BUILD.DOCS's pass predicate, and the absence of addenv in BUILD.DOCS. That is a relational read, not a per-claim verification, done by one economy agent over ~75 files with a 20-finding cap. ext: the ext comment is in its single file, but the refuting line is in Doctor.jl, outside its surface. built-html: its brief is page blurbs against @docs blocks; the rendered sentence is textually identical to source. workflow-scripts, catalogues, rulebook, templates, schemas: none of the six homes is in their reads. make.jl.seed (templates) only says a skip is exit 0, which is true. family: this is no f/f! or getter/setter pair. cold-reader: every term is defined; the failure is truth, not definition. operational-claims: it holds each docstring against ITS OWN body. frozen_rounds' body never reads GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP. `makedocs` in src is `function makedocs end`, and its body is an undocumented method in ext. The BUILD.DOCS closure is an anonymous `check!` lambda with no docstring, so the lane, which goes docstring by docstring, never visits it. The claim is about a third function, which the lane's pairing cannot express.
gaps.proposed_lens: A cross-reference/scope lane. For every sentence whose subject is another component ("the deep doctor", "gbg release", "every verb", "the wrapper"), enumerate the concrete members that subject denotes, from `Doctor.DEEP`, `VERBS` and similar. Verify the predicate on EACH member and quote a line per member. It also diffs the several homes of one claim against each other: a narrower wording in one home, here CHANGELOG, is the signal.

gaps.gap: Whole documentation surfaces that no lane reads, although they state operational claims to sessions and readers. instruments/<name>/PROTOCOL.md is injected verbatim into every instrument session (Preflight.jl:715) and rendered as guide/instruments.html. docs/make.jl hand-writes the lead paragraphs of three generated pages (doctor, instruments, rules). README.md, CHANGELOG.md and .github/workflows/*.yml are unread too. workflow-scripts reads only instruments/<name>/workflow and prelude.js. schemas reads only schema.json. pages leaves out the generated guide pages (correctly), but nothing reads their SOURCES. built-html nominally holds docs/build, but its brief narrows it to API pages and @docs blurbs.

gaps.proposed_lens: No new lens; a coverage mechanism. Make the surface map exhaustive by construction: every tracked *.md, every make.jl string literal that reaches a page, and every file `gbg preflight` injects belongs to exactly one lane. Also add a doctor/prepare check that fails when a tracked prose file is claimed by no lane.

gaps.gap: An adjective or absence claim carried by a verified count or noun phrase. The lane verifies the checkable part (a number, a name) and the qualifier rides along. The operational-claims lane owns 'what the code DOES NOT do', but only on docstrings attached to a function body. The claim sits on a MODULE docstring, a page, and a string literal rendered into consumers, and the contradicting effect happens in a child process whose code lies outside src/.
gaps.evading_example: LIVE. docs/src/index.md:63: "`gbg doctor` — 49 read-only checks". src/CLI/Doctor.jl:8 (module docstring): "The read-only health check of a consumer's tooling". src/CLI/Sync.jl:28 renders "The read-only health check of this package's tooling" into every consumer's gbg-doctor skill. Against: Doctor.jl:634-654, where BUILD.DOCS, SELF.DOCS and TEST.PKG run `docs_build`, `docs/make.jl` and `Pkg.test()`. In the tool itself, SELF.DOCS runs docs/make.jl, which overwrites docs/src/architecture.md, docs/src/guide/doctor.md, instruments.md and rules.md, rewrites docs/build, and on a CI runner reaches `deploydocs` (not suppressed: SELF.DOCS sets GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP, not GBG_ROUND). Doctor.run's own `deep` bullet (Doctor.jl:726, "they run builds, tests and witnesses") contradicts its module docstring 700 lines above. The count, 49, is exactly right.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: pages: index.md:63's checkable token is "49". `length(Doctor.CHECKS) == 49` verifies it, and "read-only" is not on the CORRECT check's quantifier list. rationale: ARCHITECTURE's §7.3 header says "read-only" too, and the project rule "a doctor check is read-only" plus the design's own admission of `--deep` child processes read as a deliberate design statement, not a defect. src: it reads Doctor.jl and may note "they run builds". But a build writing files happens in docs/make.jl, not in src/, so there is no line in its surface to quote. It is also likely read as permitted: the design admits the --deep child processes. ext and built-html: not the locus; the built page reproduces the source text. templates: the skill description is a Julia string in src/CLI/Sync.jl, not a template file. operational-claims: its 'does not do' check is per docstring against the docstring's own body. A module docstring has no body, and the writes are made by another program (make.jl) the lane does not hold. family and cold-reader: not about truth.
gaps.proposed_lens: Extend operational-claims to module docstrings and to rendered skill/page strings, with an explicit 'side-effect audit'. For every read-only, no-write, never-deploys or never-mutates claim, trace every child process the code spawns (`run`, `shell`, `pipeline`) into the program it runs, and list what that program writes.

gaps.gap: The family lane is vacuous for this package, so the relational check it stands for never runs. It is hard-wired to f/f!, getter/set_…! and physical/spectral pairs. This package has none: its ledger says its `!` functions mutate registries and it computes no physical quantity. Its real families are the several faces of one operation (`doctor`, `cmd_doctor`, `Doctor.run`; `gate`, `cmd_gate`, `frozen_rounds`; `attack`, `attack_read`) and one contract stated in several homes (the exit-code contract in README, index, verbs.md and the `main` docstring; the frozen-build skip in six places). No lane diffs the homes of one claim against each other.
gaps.evading_example: LIVE (the same fact as gap 1, found by a different lens): the frozen-build refusal claim has six homes. CHANGELOG.md:452 says "`gbg release` and the deep doctor's `SELF.DOCS`". ARCHITECTURE.md:494, index.md:29, the makedocs docstring in src/DocLints.jl, the frozen_rounds docstring at Gate.jl:77 and the ext comment all say "the deep doctor". A relational lane holding the six side by side sees one home scoping the claim more narrowly than the other five and asks why. That is the refutation. Each per-file lane reads one or two homes, each confirmed by grep, and CHANGELOG is read by nobody.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: family: it enumerates f/f!, getter/set and physical/spectral pairs. None exists, so it returns empty `checked[]` or a trivially clean result; the brief gives it nothing else to group. rationale, pages, src, ext: each holds at most two homes, each home locally confirmed (see gap 1). built-html: blurb against block. cold-reader: definitions, not agreement. operational-claims: one docstring against its own body. workflow-scripts, catalogues, rulebook, templates, schemas: out of scope.
gaps.proposed_lens: Re-parameterise `family` per package from the config. Here: 'faces of one operation' (CLI verb, in-process function, module entry), plus a 'one claim, many homes' pass that greps each distinctive contract phrase (exit codes, GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP, QUICK's definition, read-only) across ALL tracked prose and diffs the scopes.

gaps.gap: A CLEAN or low-finding lane_file is bit-for-bit indistinguishable from a lane that skimmed. `checked[]` and `candidates_found` are self-typed strings/integers with no cross-check against the surface's actual file roster or against any independent count.
gaps.evading_example: The `src` surface lane (design.md lines 39-55) is handed 76 real files in one economy-strength pass: 26 files under src/CLI/, 8 core engine files, and 42 near-identical single-purpose files under src/Scans/ (`ls src/Scans/*.jl | wc -l` = 42, e.g. src/Scans/abutting_spans.jl, mathbf.jl, xlink.jl — each a two-line comment header plus one `register_scan!` call). Nothing stops the agent from reading a fraction of those 42 nearly-identical files carefully, pattern-matching the rest, and emitting `checked: [<all 76 paths copied from its own prompt>], candidates_found: 2, findings: [2 items]`. `classify_lane` (src/CLI/Rounds.jl:343-363) accepts this as `:live` — the only two gates are (a) findings==0 and checked==[] together mean `:dead` (line 360) and (b) `candidates_found > length(findings)` means `:truncated` (line 362). Neither test can tell a genuinely-thorough 2-finding surface from an under-read one that simply never admits it under-searched — there is no comparison of `checked[]` against `lane["files"]` (the schema's own `files` array, instruments/check-docs/schema.json) anywhere in the bank path.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: This is not a per-lane content miss, it is a property of the artifact format every lane shares: the OUTPUT contract in design.md (identical text at lines 17/35/53/71/89/107/125/143/161/179) tells the agent to self-report `checked[]` and `candidates_found` but nothing external ever samples, re-runs, or hashes against what was actually read. `family`, `cold-reader` and `operational-claims` (lines 183-202) inherit the same lane_file schema and the same absence of a coverage check. The deterministic half (scans, reflection) that runs before the lanes has no analogous step either — RULE.INST.NO_TRUNCATION only binds the scan engine's literal terminal output, not an LLM lane's claimed read-completeness.
gaps.proposed_lens: Make `checked[]` a claim the harness can falsify rather than a claim the agent asserts: require the lane's tool-call log (files actually opened, e.g. via a wrapper that records Read invocations during the Workflow run) and compare its file set against `lane["files"]`; a file in the roster never opened is an automatic `:partial` status distinct from `:live`, printed in SUMMARY.md, not silently absorbed. Separately, run a periodic (not per-round) INDEPENDENT re-lane: a second, differently-seeded pass over a randomly chosen 20% of one surface's files, and compare its finding count to the original lane's count on the same files — a large, recurring gap between the two is the inter-rater-reliability signal this instrument currently has no equivalent of.

gaps.gap: Seeded recall — the design's own stated cure for self-report (PROTOCOL.md step 3: 'prints recall per class and the SUSPECT lanes') — can only ever report a number for the defect classes its own catalogue already contains, and those classes were written by the same authorship process as the lens set they calibrate. A false negative in any class the catalogue-writer did not think to plant is permanently invisible, not merely unmeasured-and-flagged.
gaps.evading_example: design.md's `operational-claims` lane (lines 191-201) lists seven distinct claim-shapes to check: a wrong stated DEFAULT, "THE" value where the body branches/mins/maxes/falls back, a wrong documented ERROR, a wrong ORDERING/TIMING claim, a wrong NO-ALLOCATION/EXACTNESS/PRESERVATION claim, a wrong ARGUMENT-effect claim, and a wrong claim about what code does NOT do. The one seed catalogue shipped in the tool, catalog/seeds/fixture.toml, has exactly eight classes: normalization, citation-drift, quantifier, notation, stale-name, cross-page, weakened-guarantee, false-property. Only the last two (an exactness claim weakened, an aliasing permission negated) touch operational-claims territory at all; the other four shapes — default-drift, branch/min/max, ordering/timing, undocumented-error — have zero seeded instances anywhere in the shipped catalogue. This is exactly the class of miss the prompt's own WHY section describes ('eight hand-specified lanes reported COMPLETE while missing an entire class'): a lane that silently cannot catch default-drift will report the identical 100%-recall summary as a lane that catches everything, because nothing ever plants a default-drift instance to test it.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: Every lane is graded, when graded at all, against the same single catalogue (PROTOCOL.md: 'plants the labelled defects of the consumer's seed catalogue... recomputes the ground truth... prints recall per class'). Since the catalogue is fixed and small, `operational-claims` cannot be shown to be blind on default-drift/branch/ordering/error-claim subtypes by this mechanism — there is no per-subtype ground truth, only per-class (and the four unrepresented subtypes fall inside classes that don't test them). No other lane or cross-check (family, cold-reader) touches recall measurement at all; recall is exclusively this one channel.
gaps.proposed_lens: Stop treating the seed catalogue as fixed background and start growing it FROM the instrument's own failures: every finding that a later `/bug-hunt`, `/audit-changes`, or an unconstrained-reader pass turns up that no check-docs lane caught becomes a new seed class in the next release (a mechanical rule, not a suggestion) so recall is measured against demonstrated blind spots, not imagined ones. Add a doctor check, e.g. `CFG.SEED_COVERAGE`, that fails when any value of the `finding.type` enum (schema.json: math, notation, structure, citation, style, operational, currency, self-containment) or any of the seven bulleted operational-claims subtypes has zero seed classes mapped to it — turning "we never tested this" from silence into a red doctor line.

gaps.gap: Severity and confidence are freeform judgment calls with zero calibration guidance anywhere in the instrument's own specification, they gate a real release-blocking decision, and — for the majority of findings, which close inside the pass budget — no independent party ever re-rates them.
gaps.evading_example: design.md, the document that IS this instrument's specification, never once mentions the words 'severity' or 'confidence' (confirmed: neither term appears anywhere in its 202 lines) — the four-level severity enum (`blocker|major|minor|nit`) and three-level confidence enum (`high|medium|low`) are filled in purely because instruments/check-docs/schema.json requires the field, with no rubric distinguishing a `blocker` from a `major` and no worked example anywhere a lane can consult. `confidence` is pure print decoration downstream: it is written to findings.md (`src/CLI/Rounds.jl:387`, `[$(f["severity"])/$(f["confidence"])]`) and to the verifier prompt (`src/CLI/Passes.jl:44`), but grep of src/CLI/Rounds.jl and src/CLI/Passes.jl finds no branch anywhere that treats a `low`-confidence finding differently from a `high`-confidence one — it costs a lane nothing to mark everything `high`. Severity is consequential (a carried `blocker`/`major` blocks a final release, per RULE.INST.CARRY as restated in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md line 2356), yet the one re-rating mechanism named in the architecture, `severity-recheck.js`, is stated in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3 as an audit-changes-only step ('audit-changes runs severity-recheck.js (anchor) before "serious" is counted'); the analogous check-docs mechanism only fires on a finding still open past the 3-pass budget ('a blind severity re-check', ARCHITECTURE.md line 2356). A finding that a lane mislabels `nit` and the fix pass happens to fix inside budget closes on the `honored` channel with no re-rating ever applied, and that `nit` label is what SUMMARY.md permanently shows a reader triaging the round.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: This sits outside every lane's brief entirely — none of the eleven per-surface lanes or three cross-cutting lanes in design.md is asked to justify or calibrate the severity/confidence it assigns; they only enumerate-and-verify content. The blind re-check exists structurally only at the CARRY boundary (past-budget survivors), so it never reaches a finding any lane rated wrong but that the fix pass still resolved on the first or second pass — which is presumably most findings.
gaps.proposed_lens: Run a blind severity re-rating at BANK time for every finding, not only for carry-time survivors: a second agent sees only the quote, the file:line and the proposed fix — never the lane's own severity/confidence — and assigns its own; a mismatch of two or more severity levels is printed in SUMMARY.md next to the finding rather than silently overwritten or silently absorbed. Give confidence a consequence: a `low`-confidence finding requires the verifier to independently confirm the quoted line still reads as claimed before it can close `honored`, rather than being fixed on the strength of an unverified read.

gaps.gap: The ten-item 'closed vocabulary' repeated verbatim in every lane brief is asserted to be ten well-formed, single-meaning concepts, but the package's own source disputes this for at least one entry, and no lane's stated algorithm is built to detect a term whose meaning silently shifts across the corpus rather than being simply undefined.
gaps.evading_example: src/CLI/Doctor.jl:14 reads: '`anchor` carries three unrelated senses across this package, and the checks below touch two.' That polysemy is live on the `pages` surface itself, which design.md hands to one lane (lines 21-37): docs/src/guide/config.md:13 uses 'anchor' for a documentation heading-reference ('references anchors, the glossary file...'), immediately followed at line 27 by an `@ref` to `GBGCodingTools.Config.resolve_anchor` (heading-resolution sense), while docs/src/guide/rules.md:592 and docs/src/guide/instruments.md:237,339,369,394 use the SAME bare word 'anchor' for 'a lane/check that stays at full strength, never economised' — a completely unrelated concept about model strength, not documentation structure. A reader of the `pages` surface who meets 'anchor' first in config.md (heading sense) and later in rules.md (economy sense) gets no signal that the word has changed meaning; both uses are individually well-formed prose.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: SELF-CONTAINED (check 2, present in every surface lane) only asks whether a term is 'bound at first use... or @ref-linked' — a one-shot boolean, not a cross-occurrence consistency check. cold-reader (lines 187-189) is explicitly ORDERED and one-directional: 'report where you FIRST meet a term, since a gloss on a later page does not close a bare use on an earlier one' — this protects against an undefined-then-defined term, never against a defined-then-redefined one; its substrate is also restricted to exported docstrings via `?name`, which does not include docs/src/guide/*.md prose at all. NOTATION (check 3) restricts its 'one symbol, one concept' rule textually to 'math variables symbolic, storage descriptive' — English terms of art are out of scope by its own wording. `family` (lines 183-185) is restricted to f/f!-style code pairs and their formula/notation, not general vocabulary. No lane, and no cross-lane step, is asked whether the SAME closed-vocabulary word means the same thing everywhere it appears.
gaps.proposed_lens: Add a twelfth cross-cutting lane (or extend `family`) scoped specifically to the ten closed-vocabulary terms: for each term, collect every sentence across every surface that uses it bare, and flag any two uses whose surrounding predicate is incompatible (a cheap first pass: does this occurrence's sentence contain a defining clause, and if two defining clauses for the same term exist anywhere in the corpus, that pair is the finding — mechanically detectable, not judgment-only). Require the ten terms to each resolve, via `@ref`, to exactly one glossary anchor, and make that link-target-uniformity a scan (deterministic), not a lane's judgment call.

gaps.gap: A flat cap of 20 findings applies identically to a one-file surface (`ext`, `rationale`) and a 76-file surface (`src`), with no size-scaling — and the one flag meant to signal 'this lane found more than it could report' actively rewards silence over honesty.
gaps.evading_example: Compare two lanes in design.md: `ext` reads one file, ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl (line 59); `src` reads 76 files (26 CLI + 8 core + 42 Scans, lines 39-55). Both get the identical instruction 'Cap at your 20 most significant' (lines 17-179, verbatim in every lane). If `src` genuinely contains 60 real self-containment gaps spread evenly across its 76 files (a plausible outcome given the 42 Scans files share one templated comment structure), a lane that HONESTLY reports `candidates_found: 60, findings: [20 items]` is marked `:truncated` by `classify_lane` (src/CLI/Rounds.jl:362, `candidates_found > n`) and named in SUMMARY.md's 'Capped lanes (candidates_found > reported; re-run narrowed if needed)' line (src/CLI/Rounds.jl:413) — a visible ding. A lane that instead reports `candidates_found: 15, findings: [15 items]` (quietly having stopped looking after the first ~20 files, or having pattern-matched the remaining Scans files as 'probably fine' without reading them) is classified `:live` (line 363) with no advisory anywhere — indistinguishable from, and strictly better-looking than, the honest lane.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: The cap and the honesty-dependent truncation flag are both defined once in the shared OUTPUT paragraph every lane inherits verbatim (design.md lines 17/35/53/…/179); no lane individually controls or can escape this incentive structure, and no downstream code (src/CLI/Rounds.jl:400-417, render_summary_md) distinguishes 'capped because genuinely thorough' from 'under-searched, so nothing to cap.'
gaps.proposed_lens: Scale the cap to the surface's real size (e.g. proportional to file count or docstring count from the deterministic pre-pass) rather than a flat 20 for every surface from 1 file to 76. Compute an independent denominator for 'how much was there to find' from a cheap mechanical count (number of docstrings, number of signature arguments, number of comment-header blocks in the surface) so `candidates_found` can be sanity-checked against a number the lane did not produce itself, rather than only against its own `findings` count.
